TrueNAS 27.0.0-RC.1: nvmet_tcp advertises MDTS=0 but rejects large transfers,NAS-144298,162587,Bug,Done,NAS,TrueNAS,software,Triage Team,62615fd89506d6006fda6bfb,TrueNAS Project Bug and Feature request tracker,,High,Complete,Ameer,62967105a0eafd0069e82ebf,Aaron Hauck,712020:11fe83eb-7de1-41b5-bcb4-6c5f62b99d45,Aaron Hauck,712020:11fe83eb-7de1-41b5-bcb4-6c5f62b99d45,07/Oct/26 5:29 PM,30/Oct/26 12:53 PM,,30/Oct/26 12:52 PM,27.0.0-RC.1,Master - TrueNAS Nightlies,SCALE-25.10.8 (Goldeye),27.0.0,28.0.0-BETA.1,SCALE-25.10.8 (Goldeye),,Middleware,,1,COMMUNITY_USER,,,"Summary

After upgrading from TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.7 to 27.0.0-RC.1, the kernel NVMe-oF TCP target (nvmet_tcp) advertises MDTS = 0 (no transfer size limit). It then rejects large transfers with status sct 0x0 / sc 0xf (Data SGL Length Invalid, DNR set), and the target logs nvmet_tcp: queue N: failed to map data. A Linux initiator follows the advertised MDTS, raises max_sectors_kb to 32768 and sends single I/Os of up to 32 MiB. All 137 failed I/Os still in the initiator's log were between 4.23 and 32 MiB.

On the initiator, a host-mounted ext4 filesystem aborted its journal and remounted read-only, and writes in flight were lost. Severity: high. Data is lost silently on a supported block-sharing path, with no warning on the TrueNAS side apart from the kernel log.
Environment
The target is TrueNAS SCALE 27.0.0-RC.1, running as a KVM guest on the Proxmox host that is also the initiator. The two talk NVMe/TCP over a 10 GbE VLAN.
Component
Target (TrueNAS)
Initiator (Proxmox VE)
Version
TrueNAS SCALE 27.0.0-RC.1, upgraded from 25.10.7 on 2026-10-07
pve-manager 9.2.20
Kernel
6.18.52-production+truenas
Tooling
Kernel nvmet (nvmet.global.config: kernel: true, ana: false, rdma: false)
nvme-cli 2.13, libnvme 1.13, native multipath (nvme_core.multipath=Y)
Hardware
KVM VM: 8 vCPU, 16 GiB RAM, AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370 host. Pools on PCI-passthrough SATA controller and 2× NVMe.
Same physical host
Port
TCP, IPv4, 4420. param_inline_data_size 16384, param_max_queue_size 1024, param_pi_enable 0
24 I/O queues per controller
Subsystems
3 (nqn.2026-09.org.freenas.ctl:truenas-{nvme,hdd,ssd2}), attr_version 2.1, attr_model ""TrueNAS KVM VM""
Connected to all 3
Namespaces
7 ZVOLs, 16K volblocksize, lz4, sync standard (on a mirror and a single-disk pool)
Used as Proxmox VM disks and LXC rootfs (ext4 mounted on the host)
Firmware revision reported
Steps to reproduce
The failure was observed under real workloads (an ext4 rootfs under docker pull). The isolated test in steps 4–5 has not yet been run on a scratch namespace.
1. On TrueNAS 27.0.0-RC.1, create a ZVOL and share it over NVMe-oF TCP (kernel target) on port 4420.
2. From a Linux initiator, connect with nvme connect -t tcp -a <target> -s 4420 -n <subnqn>.
3. Check what the initiator negotiated: nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvmeX
column2: grep mdts returns 0. /sys/block/nvmeXnY/queue/max_hw_sectors_kb is 2147483647, and max_sectors_kb is 32768.

column1: 4. Issue one large direct write to the scratch namespace (this destroys data on it): dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvmeXnY bs=16M count=4 oflag=direct.
5. Expected failure: dd returns EIO. The initiator logs I/O Error (sct 0x0 / sc 0xf) DNR, and the target logs nvmet_tcp: queue N: failed to map data.
6. Control: echo 1024 > /sys/block/nvmeXnY/queue/max_sectors_kb, plus the same on the hidden path device nvmeXcZnY, then repeat step 4. It succeeds.
Expected vs actual behaviour
Expected
Actual
Advertised limit

MDTS = 0 (unlimited)
Large I/O (≥ 4.23 MiB observed)

Rejected with sc 0xf Data SGL Length Invalid, DNR set, so it is never retried
Target log
Silent, or a clear message naming the limit
nvmet_tcp: queue N: failed to map data, 2,308 lines in ~25 minutes, no size given
Small I/O
Completes
Completes
Evidence
The target advertises no limit, the initiator sizes its queue from that, and only multi-megabyte transfers fail. Small I/O on the same queues completes normally.
Initiator, negotiated limits (identical on all three controllers):
$ nvme id-ctrl /dev/nvme1
mdts      : 0
$ cat /sys/block/nvme1n5/queue/{max_hw_sectors_kb,max_sectors_kb,max_segments}
Initiator kernel log (first failure 10:23:45, ext4 abort 10:43:00):
nvme1c1n5: I/O Cmd(0x1) @ LBA 156172288, 52168 blocks, I/O Error (sct 0x0 / sc 0xf) DNR
I/O error, dev nvme1c1n5, sector 156172288 op 0x1:(WRITE) flags 0x2000800 phys_seg 5434 prio class 2
EXT4-fs (nvme1n5): failed to convert unwritten extents to written extents -- potential data loss!  (inode 3284128, error -5)
nvme1c1n5: I/O Cmd(0x1) @ LBA 136049168, 38848 blocks, I/O Error (sct 0x0 / sc 0xf) DNR
Buffer I/O error on dev nvme1n5, logical block 17006146, lost sync page write
Aborting journal on device nvme1n5-8.
EXT4-fs error (device nvme1n5): ext4_journal_check_start:86: comm dockerd: Detected aborted journal
EXT4-fs (nvme1n5): Remounting filesystem read-only
Target kernel log (2,308 lines, last at 10:48:00, none after the initiator cap was applied):
nvmet_tcp: queue 21: failed to map data
nvmet_tcp: queue 64: failed to map data
nvmet_tcp: queue 19: failed to map data
Failed I/Os by size (137 still in the initiator's ring buffer, 512-byte LBAs; every status was sct 0x0 / sc 0xf):
Size
Reads
Writes
4–8 MiB
8–16 MiB
Smallest failure 4.23 MiB, largest 32 MiB (the initiator's max_sectors_kb). The largest size that succeeds was not measured.

Connection event before the failures: the target VM rebooted for the upgrade. At 07:34:46 all three controllers hit an admin keep-alive timeout, and they reconnected at 07:35:48 (attempt 5/60). Errors began at 10:23, under heavy writes.
Analysis
The target enforces a transfer-size limit that it does not advertise. This is our reading of the evidence; we have not traced the code.

• failed to map data comes from the data-mapping step of nvmet_tcp, which runs before any I/O reaches the ZVOL. The pools stayed healthy (zpool status -x: all pools healthy) and no ZFS errors were logged.
• sc 0xf with DNR means the target judged the request's data length invalid. A transient failure such as a failed allocation would more likely show as an internal error (sc 0x6) without DNR.
• MDTS = 0 tells the host there is no limit, so the Linux initiator allows up to 32 MiB per request. Capping the initiator at 1 MiB stopped the errors immediately on both sides.

• Regression: the same initiator, namespaces and workload ran from 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-07 on TrueNAS 25.10.7 without these errors. We did not record MDTS or max_sectors_kb under 25.10.7, so we can't say whether the advertised value changed or the target's internal limit did.
Possible contributors to check: the 16 GiB RAM of the target VM (if the limit depends on memory), and the 16 KiB inline_data_size (it only applies to in-capsule data, so it probably isn't the cause).
Impact
One host filesystem went read-only and lost writes. Every other consumer of the target was exposed to the same failure.

• Filesystem damage: the LXC rootfs (ext4 on the namespace) aborted its journal and remounted emergency_ro. Writes in flight were lost; ext4 named one file explicitly. e2fsck -f afterwards had to clear orphaned inodes and fix free block and inode counts.
• Service impact: about 20 minutes of application failures, no container image pulls, and a full outage of the container host for the fsck.
• No signal on the target: no alert, and nothing in the UI or the middleware. The only trace is a kernel log line that gives no size.
• Wider exposure: VM disks on the same subsystems are exposed too. Inside a guest, the error surfaces as a guest-side I/O error.
Workaround
Capping the initiator at 1 MiB per request stops the failures. The target has logged no further errors since the cap was applied at about 10:53 on 2026-10-07.

With native NVMe multipath, the limit must be set on the head device and on each hidden path device (nvmeXcYnZ). The block layer merges requests on the path device up to the path's own limit. Path devices emit no uevents, so a udev rule has to reach them through the head device's multipath/ links:
# /etc/udev/rules.d/99-truenas-nvmeof-max-sectors.rules
ACTION==""add
column2: change"", SUBSYSTEM==""block"", ENV{DEVTYPE}==""disk"", KERNEL==""nvme*n*"", ATTRS{subsysnqn}==""nqn.2026-09.org.freenas.ctl:*"", ATTR{queue/max_sectors_kb}=""1024"", RUN+=""/bin/sh -c 'for q in /sys/block/%k/multipath/*/queue/max_sectors_kb; do [ -e $$q ] && echo 1024 > $$q; done'""

column1: 1 MiB is a conservative choice. The largest size that still works was not established.
Suggested fix and attachments
The target should advertise its real limit, so that initiators never send a transfer it will reject.
• Set MDTS on the TrueNAS NVMe-oF subsystems to the largest transfer nvmet_tcp can map, or lift the internal limit back to what 25.10.7 accepted.

Dataset passphrase exposed in plaintext in core.get_jobs arguments of internal zfs.dataset.bulk_process (check_key) jobs,NAS-144783,163164,Bug,Done,NAS,TrueNAS,software,Triage Team,62615fd89506d6006fda6bfb,TrueNAS Project Bug and Feature request tracker,,Blocker,Complete,Vladimir Vinogradenko,60d3201794692800700f4222,Arnold Gossard,62bef2abd8658e0d491adbdf,Arnold Gossard,62bef2abd8658e0d491adbdf,20/Oct/26 1:03 PM,22/Oct/26 7:53 AM,,22/Oct/26 7:53 AM,SCALE-25.10.7 (Goldeye),,,SCALE-25.10.8 (Goldeye),,,,,,0,COMMUNITY_USER,,,"When a passphrase-encrypted dataset is unlocked from the web UI, the UI first calls pool.dataset.encryption_summary to validate the passphrase. That method spawns an internal zfs.dataset.bulk_process job with the check_key operation, and the passphrase is stored unredacted in that job’s arguments:
1272 zfs.dataset.bulk_process [""check_key"", [[""<dataset>"", {""key"": null}]]]
1274 zfs.dataset.bulk_process [""check_key"", [[""<dataset>"", {""key"": ""<PASSPHRASE IN CLEAR>""}]]]

The parent job pool.dataset.unlock correctly masks the passphrase as ********. The redaction is therefore inconsistent: the secret is protected in the public job but leaked by the internal job created in the same flow.
The entry stays in the in-memory job history, readable through core.get_jobs by FULL_ADMIN sessions, until middlewared restarts.
Relevant code (25.10.7):
middlewared/plugins/zfs_/dataset_encryption.py:187-188: @job() def bulk_process(self, job, name: str, params: list). The params argument is untyped, so no Secret redaction applies.
middlewared/plugins/pool_/dataset_encryption_info.py:111: encryption_summary passes user-supplied keys/passphrases to bulk_process('check_key', ...).

middlewared/plugins/pool_/dataset_encryption_info.py:190: sync_db_keys calls the same path daily with keys from the database. Hex keys of key-encrypted datasets are likely exposed the same way (not verified, no key-encrypted datasets on this system).
Steps to reproduce
Create or lock a passphrase-encrypted dataset.
Unlock it from the web UI (Datasets → Unlock).
Run midclt call core.get_jobs '[[""method"",""="",""zfs.dataset.bulk_process""]]'.
Observe the passphrase in plaintext in arguments.
Expected
Passphrases and keys are redacted in all job arguments, including internal jobs, consistent with pool.dataset.unlock.
Actual
Passphrase visible in clear in zfs.dataset.bulk_process job arguments.
Impact
Low to medium. Only FULL_ADMIN sessions can read internal jobs, so this is not privilege escalation. However:
Passphrases are deliberately not stored by TrueNAS. This bug makes a secret recoverable that is designed to be unrecoverable, even by an administrator.

Reading job history is a routine, read-only diagnostic operation that users don’t treat as sensitive. Its output is routinely shared or forwarded: pasted into forum posts or support tickets, logged by monitoring scripts that record failed jobs, and increasingly consumed by AI assistants / MCP integrations with API or SSH access. In those cases the passphrase silently leaves the system and ends up in third-party transcripts and logs. This happened in practice while diagnosing an unrelated app upgrade failure with an AI agent.
The same passphrase often protects copies outside the system (raw-replicated targets, offsite copies), so exposure is not limited to the local dataset.
Suggested fix
Type the params of zfs.dataset.bulk_process (or at least the check_key payload) with Secret fields, so the existing redaction mechanism applies.
Or, more generally: redact arguments of internal jobs in core.get_jobs output for external clients by default, mirroring the existing raw_result behaviour for result.
Or avoid passing the raw key into a job at all: perform check_key synchronously without job bookkeeping.

column1: Raise the default TNC client timeout to 55 seconds on 25.10,NAS-144031,162155,Bug,Done,NAS,TrueNAS,software,Triage Team,62615fd89506d6006fda6bfb,TrueNAS Project Bug and Feature request tracker,,High,Complete,Caleb St. John,60d31fa194692800700f3c5c,Zack,60d3201cf6505400695a071f,Zack,60d3201cf6505400695a071f,22/Sep/26 3:23 PM,05/Oct/26 10:59 AM,,05/Oct/26 10:59 AM,SCALE-25.10.7 (Goldeye),,,SCALE-25.10.8 (Goldeye),,,,Middleware,,0,hf_want,IX_EMPLOYEE,triage_skipped,"Every call a 25.10 system makes to TrueNAS Connect's account service runs under the 15-second default in truenas_connect_utils. Only the websocket authenticator sets its own 30-second budget. The service often cannot answer the ACME read inside 15 seconds when the primary certificate authority is slow or hung. ZeroSSL's nonce endpoint takes 8 to 9 seconds of server time in normal operation, and the failover to Let's Encrypt on the service side is sized for a caller that waits 55 seconds. When the read times out the middleware marks certificate generation failed and does not retry, so the user's only path forward is to re-register and hope for the best, often with multiple failures in a row before abandoning adoption.
Production data on 25.10 registrations that never sent a heartbeat, by week, against a baseline of about 5 percent before August:

column5: 25.10 registrations

column1: Every backend change shipped or planned for this path is invisible to a 25.10 system until the client waits long enough for it, and enterprise adoption keeps 25.10 in the field into 2027. The change is truenas_connect_utils commit 10aa83b, on master since 2026-05-06 and in every 26.0 build, which raises the default in the request helper from 15 to 55 seconds. It is one line and cherry-picks onto stable/goldeye. 55 seconds sits above every TrueNAS Connect route deadline, under the 60-second gateway cutoff, and under the 120-second heartbeat interval. Without this change, TrueNAS Connect cannot be made reliable for 25.10 systems from the backend alone.",,;05/Oct/26 10:59 AM;ug:0672c7af-e0d3-4630-9e94-1e500d09260b;600,,0,0,600,,0,0,600,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,ApprovalsCFValue{approvals=[]},,0.0,,,,,,,,,,,Low,,,,,,,,Event Example,,,,,,,,Kristy Mao,712020:31726e18-f157-4558-94b1-012f6a300a75,,,,,,No,,High,,,,,,,,,,,Standard,,,,,,,,,Yes,,,,,,Not Tested,,,,,,,,,0

Existing App keeps invalid NVIDIA GPU UUID after GPU replacement (TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.4),NAS-142006,159490,Bug,Done,NAS,TrueNAS,software,Triage Team,62615fd89506d6006fda6bfb,TrueNAS Project Bug and Feature request tracker,,Low,Complete,Muhammad,61815dc55800630069e7bff2,lucas compagnucci,712020:673b3995-45aa-47fb-ac50-fa1560d6eeb0,lucas compagnucci,712020:673b3995-45aa-47fb-ac50-fa1560d6eeb0,29/Jul/26 5:22 PM,02/Oct/26 11:39 AM,,02/Oct/26 11:39 AM,SCALE-25.10.4 (Goldeye),,,27.0.0-RC.1,28.0.0-BETA.1,SCALE-25.10.8 (Goldeye),,Apps,,0,COMMUNITY_USER,hf_want,ready_for_assignment,"Hello,
I believe I found a bug related to NVIDIA GPU assignment in TrueNAS SCALE 25.10.4.
Background
My system was originally using an NVIDIA RTX 3080.
I later replaced it with an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti.
The NVIDIA driver was reinstalled correctly, and the new GPU is detected without any issues.
The following commands report the correct GPU UUID:
nvidia-smi -L
midclt call app.gpu_choices
Both report:
Problem
An existing Plex application (plex2) worked before the GPU replacement.
After replacing the GPU, enabling GPU acceleration from the Apps UI causes the container to fail during startup with:
failed to create shim task:
failed to get device handle from UUID:
Not Found
Inspecting the application configuration shows that it still contains a different GPU UUID:
resources"": {
""gpus"": {
""nvidia_gpu_selection"": {
""use_gpu"": true,
That UUID does not exist anymore.
Docker receives this stale UUID through DeviceRequests and NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, causing container creation to fail.
Additional observations
Docker GPU support works correctly.
docker run --gpus all ... nvidia-smi works correctly.
The middleware correctly detects the current GPU and its UUID.
Creating a new Plex application (plex3) and assigning the same GPU works perfectly.
This suggests that existing application configurations may retain an obsolete GPU UUID after a GPU replacement, and editing the application from the UI does not refresh it with the current UUID.
Expected behavior
When an existing application is edited and an NVIDIA GPU is selected, the stored GPU UUID should be updated to match the current UUID reported by app.gpu_choices.
I hope this information helps identify the issue.
Thank you.
